meta.classesChecked: Class perks per the EA forums class-perk overview (Sept 2026).
meta.mapsNote: Map multipliers and per-legend map fit are first-pass defaults; tune them to taste.

perks.name: Battle Surge
perks.effect: Breaking an enemy's shield boosts sprint and reload speed.

perks.name: Stowed Reload
perks.effect: Stowed weapons reload automatically after a short delay.

perks.name: Trailblazer
perks.effect: Allies get a speed boost when running toward you from long distances.

perks.name: Care Package Insight
perks.effect: Reveals a care package's contents, including its best item.

perks.name: Charged Knock

perks.name: Survey Beacons
perks.effect: Scanning a Survey Beacon briefly reveals nearby enemy positions.

perks.name: Threat Vision
perks.effect: Threat vision while aiming down sights.

perks.name: Revive Expert
perks.effect: Faster revives (not D.O.C.), revives provide health regen. Banner crafting & ally deathboxes spawn Mobile Respawn Beacon

perks.name: Zone Overcharge

rotate.label: Team rotation
rotate.missing: Nothing to move the whole squad. Rotate early and mindfully or you'll be caught by the ring or third parties.
rotate.strong: Moves as one, so it can rotate early and choose where fights happen.

intel.label: Intel
intel.missing: No recon. You'll be guessing where enemies are, so play off audio and pings.
intel.strong: Plenty of recon: you should know where teams are before you commit.

engage.label: Engage
engage.missing: No tool to start fights. You'll rely on raw gunplay & positioning to take good trades.
engage.strong: Has the tools to start fights on your own terms and punish mistakes fast.

disengage.label: Disengage
disengage.missing: No way out of a bad fight. Commit carefully and don't over-peek.
disengage.strong: Can back out of a bad fight instead of dying in it.

zone.label: Zone control
zone.missing: Can't deny open ground. Pushes across open space will be hard to stop.
zone.strong: Can deny open ground and split up a push.

hold.label: Building lockdown
hold.missing: Can't fortify a building. Late-game holds will rely on gunplay & well-timed repositioning.
hold.strong: Can lock down a building and make it miserable to push.

sustain.label: Sustain
sustain.missing: No team heals or shields. Long fights favour the other team.
sustain.strong: Out-heals the other team when fights drag on.

cover.label: Deployable cover
cover.missing: No on-demand cover. Open ground in endgame is dangerous.
cover.strong: Brings its own cover for open endgames.

revive.label: Safe revives
revive.missing: No protected or quick revives. A knock is often a lost player.
revive.strong: A knock doesn't have to be a death: revives can more easily be played around.

damage.label: Ability damage
damage.missing: Little ability damage. Poke with grenades to soften teams.
damage.strong: Chips teams down with abilities before the guns come out.

mobility.label: Personal mobility
mobility.missing: No personal mobility, foresight & positioning is crucial for all members

breach.label: Breach
breach.missing: No way to crack a fortified building. Bunkered teams in endgame will be hard to dislodge.
breach.strong: Can crack a fortified building and force a team out.

kings-canyon.name: Kings Canyon
kings-canyon.blurb: Mid-sized, with lots of choke points and tight interiors.

worlds-edge.name: World's Edge
worlds-edge.blurb: A mix of wide open stretches and dense towns; rotations are long.

olympus.name: Olympus
olympus.blurb: Open, with long sightlines and exposed endgames.

storm-point.name: Storm Point
storm-point.blurb: The largest map. Steep hills, long rotations and long-range fights.

broken-moon.name: Broken Moon
broken-moon.blurb: Large craters linked by zip rails. Open spaces punctuated by open buildings

e-district.name: E-District
